verificationLegend.SOURCE_PAGE_SUPPORTED: Relevant published source explicitly supports the modest claim; not a scholarly signoff.
verificationLegend.SOURCE_PAGE_SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS: Source page supports part of claim but editorial and item-collation limits remain.

GHDI_MARBURG.kind: edited primary text in English translation
GHDI_MARBURG.anchor: Marburg Articles, date header, arts. 1–15, source colophon

claims.claim: The fifteen Marburg Articles are dated 3 October 1529 and bear signatories.
claims.expertQuestion: Check original-date variants, signatories, and the wording of 'written and signed'.

claims.claim: The first fourteen articles contain shared positions; Article 15 also records agreement on parts of the Lord's Supper.
claims.anchor: Articles 1–15, especially first two sentences of 15
claims.expertQuestion: Verify how many distinct propositions in Article 15 were shared and avoid saying 'the fifteenth was entirely disputed'.

claims.claim: Article 15 explicitly leaves unresolved whether Christ's true body and blood are bodily present in bread and wine.
claims.expertQuestion: Compare German wording of bodily presence and subsequent historiographic interpretation.

claims.claim: Article 15 calls for mutual Christian love and prayer despite the unresolved difference.
claims.expertQuestion: Distinguish the text's exhortation from claims about historical reconciliation.

claims.claim: The Augsburg Confession was presented on 25 June 1530 at the Diet of Augsburg.
claims.expertQuestion: Cross-check German/Latin presentation procedures and submitted document identity.

claims.claim: A confession submitted at the 1530 Diet should not be treated as an identical physical object to 1530 printed copies.
claims.expertQuestion: Check surviving presentation manuscripts versus known 1530 copies; discriminate physical exemplar from text.

claims.claim: The Gruber catalogue reports six German and one Latin unauthorized 1530 editions.
claims.expertQuestion: Verify edition count, what counts as an edition, and whether wording 'unofficial' is justified.

claims.claim: The Gruber catalogue identifies 1531 printings containing the Augsburg Confession and its Apology, separately in Latin and German.
claims.expertQuestion: Identify edition chronology and distinguish individual 1531 imprints and translations.

claims.claim: The 1531 event's Augsburg place label is topical and must not be represented as the confirmed place of printing for all copies.
claims.anchor: Gruber 46 Witebergae imprint; Gruber 7 November colophon
claims.expertQuestion: Verify original imprint places by physical-object catalogue and adjust UI label if misunderstood.

claims.claim: Gruber 28 is identified as a 1540 Variata edition with a changed formulation of Article X on the Lord's Supper.
claims.expertQuestion: Collate Latin wording across 1531, 1540 and confession edition; document changes precisely.

claims.claim: The Gruber catalogue also describes a 1540 copy it explicitly says is not Variata.
claims.anchor: Paragraph following the Gruber 28 entry; item number not identified there
claims.expertQuestion: Recover the specific item number/imprint and confirm whether the two 1540 works are separate physical items and which texts were compared.

claims.claim: An edited/translated Marburg document and a rare-book collection catalogue provide different types of evidence; neither alone completes a direct original-copy collation.
claims.anchor: GHDI source/translator colophon versus Gruber item descriptions
claims.expertQuestion: Ensure UI distinguishes manuscript witness, print, editorial translation, holdings description, and own summary.

claims.claim: Do not infer all Lutheran/Reformed confessional acceptance of the 1540 Variata solely from item descriptions.
claims.expertQuestion: Review 1540/1580 reception with multiple modern scholarly sources and differentiate later confessional positions.

claims.claim: The Gruber description's claim of compromise with 'Calvinists' is a retrospective interpretive label, not a 1540 self-description that can be copied verbatim into the UI.
claims.expertQuestion: Confirm chronology and historiographic appropriateness of labeling 1540 interlocutors 'Calvinists'.

reviewWorkflow.note: Legacy claim IDs are contextual holds; no unverified one-to-one claim mapping is asserted.
reviewWorkflow.freezePolicy: Do not modify original approved-looking historical prose or lift canShip until qualified historians review the high-risk claims.
